reading:
The trued line is the tour's most complete system. On the landing panel it was #1 at 7.96, ahead of Desk Terminal, Joined's 7.54. The judges love its single line language: terminus, ring stops, T buffer, one lamp at now. It runs through the greeting's steel branch of starters, Coming up's rail with plates that carry a kind ring, a sunk mono time well and who it is for, the setup route, To do's timetable margin, Status's glass strip of lamp banks with its 'Who answers' chain, and Settings. They also love that the light is held to the greeting board: E7 pool, raster, E4 halo, the box turning #6dff9c while someone types, and 'plan' with a hot core. Everything else is calm slate and steel. Squint at it and you see the page's content, not a wash.

Four things keep it from winning, and every lens names at least one:
- The subway map. The Plans month runs a rail with lamps under every week (system, usability, feedback, style, all in both rounds).
- The Next up tube is cramped as plate one. It is 'of another species', and the lit run is only a stub (soul, skeptic, feedback, system).
- 'Finish setting up' takes a whole three-column board and pushes To do below the fold (interaction, skeptic, style, usability).
- The navy-slate plates read as a blue 'UI kit' (skeptic, feedback).

Smaller faults: plate names break inside proper names ('Mount St. / Helens'); the To do margin invents '19:56' times; Ideas is the one page with no line art or phosphor; Status leads with a $0.00 block where judges want an instrument; and on the phone the Coming up rail runs under the fold and the chevron in 'who is asking?' is cramped.

To win, keep the system and the starter branch exactly. Make the tube the hero again as the line's lit head. Take one rail off each page where it is not an order, and add one instrument and one visible afterglow. That way the main camp's strengths (Desk Terminal's needle and month trace, Quote Board's one-line setup and the row afterglow that shows) arrive in the track's own steel and lamps.

briefs.name: Trued, Headlamp
briefs.hypothesis: Trued, Relit already has the most complete system on any panel. Its losses were local and named: the month's subway rails, the cramped tube, the setup board and the navy plates. Each fix below is one the lenses asked for. Each graft from the main camp fills a hole the judges named: an instrument on Status, one lit trace on the month, a one-line setup and a hover that registers. The graft replaces something rather than sitting beside it, so the page gets calmer and more lit where it matters at once. That should lift soul (the tube is the hero, the run is longer, there is light on Plans and Status), interaction and usability (To do above the fold, the month a grid again) and the skeptic (no navy, no subway map), while keeping the system and style scores that put it first.
briefs.brief:
Start from t3-track-refine2's files: x14a-a/variants/t3-track-refine2/templates/*, sheet.css, and src/trued.css, relit.css, relight.css, phosphor.css, track.css and branch.css, rebuilt with src/build.py. Keep the line language unchanged: terminus, ring stops, T buffer and one lamp at now. Keep the palette's ground, the Archivo/DM Sans/DM Mono trio and the bar.

HOME, greeting board (.board):
- Keep the board exactly as it is: the E7 pool and raster, the E4 halo on the box, the box turning #6dff9c while someone types, and the steel branch of starters on the right with ring stops and full-width arrowed keys.
- Title: 'Tell Vera what needs a *plan*.' The full stop goes inside the title's own run, after the lit span. Set it at clamp(2.25rem, 4vw, 3rem), Archivo 700 at about 88% stretch, with text-wrap: balance. Only 'plan' is lit, carrying E1 with its hot core. The rest is at full --heading ink.
- Grow the box to fill the board's height, so the title has scale and the lower half is not empty.
- 'Or start with' becomes the branch's terminus label. Set it as a real label (DM Sans 600, 0.8125rem, --ink-2, sentence case, no tracking) sitting on the terminus bar where the branch leaves the box, so the branch reads as starting at the question.
- Each starter key gets a quiet second line in --ink-3 at 0.8125rem: 'usually lands in Plans', 'in To do', 'in Ideas'.
- Phone: give the select's chevron 0.75rem of right padding from 'who is asking?'.

HOME, setup (.panel.setup becomes section.setup-line):
- Replace the three-column board with one band, 3.5-4rem high, set on the slate tray. No amber outline and no amber fill.
- Contents, left to right:
  - a small amber lamp (6px, amber only here) and 'Finish setting up' in --ink-2;
  - a short steel stub carrying three 0.875rem ring stops, the first lit #6dff9c with E4 and numbered 1/2/3 in DM Mono;
  - step 1's link at body size ('Choose your own password, so everybody signs in as themselves');
  - after it, 'then Telegram · Google Calendar' in --ink-3, as words, not a fold;
  - a T buffer, then 'All 3 steps →' at the right.
- Phone: two lines (stub and lamp, then the link).

HOME, Coming up (.coming.tray, ol.line.across.agenda):
- The Next up tube leaves the plate row and becomes the line's lit head. It stands at full height, 4:3 at about 22rem wide, on the left of the band. Keep the parent's tube markup: NEXT UP, the title, the time, '3 more on the line' and the radar.
- From the tube's chin a 2px phosphor drop (the power wire) falls onto the rail's first lit stop.
- The lit run (--on, E2 glow) goes from the 'now' lamp through the tube's stop to the second stop (Mount St. Helens). From there the rail is steel.
- The three .stop-plate plates sit to the right of the tube, from the rail.
  - Recolour them from navy (--ink-plate) to neutral graphite: about #15191a, chroma at most 0.01, 1px steel edge. Drop the cyan cap; the kind's colour lives only in its .kind-ring.
  - Tighten them to their content: kind label, name, then one line with who and the sunk time well (.well) together, so there is no empty middle.
  - Names: one size down (0.9375rem/1.25 Archivo 650). Use text-wrap: pretty, never a line clamp that cuts. Pass names through a nbsp filter in views.py (or a template filter) that joins 'St.' and initials to the next word, so 'Mount St. Helens' never breaks inside the name.
  - Shorten the Google note to one line ('Google not connected: these are the bot's plans'), one leading step under the head.
- Phone: the tube goes full width first, then the stops stack vertically down a left rail (date figure in the margin, plate beside it). No sideways rail cut off under the fold.

HOME, To do and Lately added: they now rise above the fold on a 1280px laptop.
- To do margin: the date only, figure then 'Oct' over 'Sun', both in DM Mono at one size, in --ink-3. Show a clock time only when one was set (never the invented '19:56'). Widen the gutter to 1.25rem so 'now' does not crowd the lamps.
- 'now' is a 13px label.
- Put the count and '3 late' (amber words, a link) on the H2's baseline.

BAR: add a 'Home' key before 'Vera' with the house icon, the same style as the others.

PLANS month (plans_month.html, .month-board):
- Delete the per-week rails and their lamps (.run, .run-on, the week .now-run). The grid is a grid again.
- Today's cell gets a 1px #6dff9c outline with E4 and a 'now' label.
- Each day holding a plan carries a small ring before its day numeral.
- Above the grid, under the month head, put one glass strip about 4.5rem high (the .crt material, scanlines and the E6 bloom). It is the month drawn as one track: 1-31 as ticks in DM Mono at 11px, a lit lamp at today, a lit run from today to the next plan only, and a ring at each plan day carrying the same day numeral as its cell, so the mark joins the strip to the grid. Past plan days are dim rings.
- Plans list: unchanged except for the graphite plates.

IDEAS (ideas.html): put back the line from home over the table, one tube wide. The listed places are stations on a line from a lit 'home' terminus, ordered by drive time, each station numbered to its table row (No.). Keep the table, filters and head row as they are.

STATUS (status.html, .instrument and the glass strip):
- The strip's left cell becomes a moving-coil spend meter on the glass. Its arc scale runs from 0 to the day's limit, with labels at $1.00 and $2.00 in VT323, a dashed limit tick and a ghost needle at the week's peak (average day), so a still never shows a bare needle at zero. The needle swings in on load.
- Keep 'SPENT TODAY, ABOUT $0.00' as a small figure in the glass's top corner.
- Add scanlines and a breathing power lamp at its chin.
- Keep the three lamp banks and the tally row, with counts in wheat/bone and amber only for 'needs a look'.
- Keep the 'Who answers' chain.

EVERY PAGE, the row afterglow:
- Pointing at a row lights it at once: plates, To do rows, Ideas rows, Lately added rows, Settings rows and the starter keys.
- The light is a 12% steel wash (--row-wash), a 2px inset sage-to-phosphor edge and an 18px soft halo, coming on in 0.12s and decaying over 1.4s.
- On the starter keys the ring stop beside the key also lights.
- Apply it on :has(:focus-visible) too.
- prefers-reduced-motion: no decay, instant.

Keep everywhere else: focus rings (restore the select's), 44px targets, CSP-safe CSS only, and sentence-case labels. Update the design's STYLE notes for the graphite plate token, the setup line and the month strip.
briefs.borrows:
OWN JUDGES' FIXES (most cited first):
- (1) Plans month: drop the per-week rails, light only today and mark plan days. Asked by system, usability, feedback and style on the landing panel, and by feedback, system and usability in tour round 3.
- (2) Fold 'Finish setting up' to one line. Interaction (twice), skeptic, style and usability.
- (3) Give the tube its height back and make it the line's lit head, with Sill Line's tube-to-rail drop. Soul, skeptic (twice), feedback and system.
- (4) Light the run at least to the second stop. Soul and skeptic.
- (5) Navy plates to neutral graphite with a steel edge, darker so the tube is the one bright thing. Skeptic (twice) and feedback.
- (6) Plate names balanced by words, no break inside 'Mount St. Helens', set one size down. Feedback, style, interaction, type and usability.
- (7) Greeting headline up to about 3rem. Style (twice) and feedback.
- (8) 'Or start with' as the branch's terminus and a real label. System and type.
- (9) The Ideas line from home. Feedback, style and system.
- (10) To do margin: date only in --ink-3, no invented times, the count and late on the H2 baseline, 'now' at 13px. System, type and usability.
- (11) Phone: stops stacked vertically, room for the chevron, a one-line Google note. Feedback, interaction and usability.
- (12) A Home item in the bar. Usability.
- (13) The starter keys' 'usually lands in' second line. Interaction, from timetable-refine.

OTHER CAMP'S FEATURES, rebuilt native:
- (A) Desk Terminal, Joined (r13-idea-1): the moving-coil spend needle on Status, with the round-13 lesson's fix of a limit tick and a ghost peak. Source: x14a-a/variants/r13-idea-1/templates/_ui.html, macro spend_meter (line 235); templates/status.html, lines 53-69 (crt('readout spend-meter'), spend_meter(used, per_day/limit, limit)); sheet.css .spend-meter .crt-tube (3077), .needle-core/.needle-halo/.needle-tip/.needle-ghost/.needle and @keyframes swing (3095-3100). Rebuilt in trued's own glass strip, in place of the $0.00 block, with track-style scale ticks (it answers system, style, skeptic and soul asking for an instrument).
- (B) Desk Terminal, Joined (r13-idea-1): the Plans glass trace of the month. Source: templates/plans_month.html line 37 (crt('next-up plan-trace')) and sheet.css .plan-trace (3037-3038, 3239-3245). Rebuilt as one track strip of the month, with ring marks carrying the cells' day numerals and a lit run from today to the next plan. It replaces the per-week rails.
- (C) Quote Board at Evening (r13-mut-3, ledger L270): setup folded to one line naming the next step. Source: x14a-a/variants/r13-mut-3/templates/home.html, lines 126-140 (section.alert.setup, .alert-figure, .alert-one, the 'All N steps' fold); sheet.css .alert-figure and .alert-one. Rebuilt as a short steel stub of three ring stops with step 1 lit. The other two steps are kept as words rather than a fold (the ledger's middle way), and amber is held to one small lamp, not a figure or an outline.
- (D) Quote Board at Evening (r13-mut-3, ledger L228): the row afterglow that shows. Source: x14a-a/variants/r13-mut-3/sheet.css --row-wash (line 72), --afterglow (line 92), and .tape > li:hover (1271), .idea-rows > li.card:hover (1468) and .task:hover (1620). Rebuilt on the track's plates, rows and starter keys, with :has(:focus-visible), and a sage edge so hover never reads as a live state. This is soul's 'branch tips glow faintly on hover'.

OWN CAMP, the fix's source: Sill Line, Ticked (t3-track-graft) for the tube-to-rail drop and the Ideas line from home: x14a-b/variants/t3-track-graft/templates/ideas.html, lines 77-104 (.from-home-text, svg.home-line).
briefs.title: Tell Vera what needs a *plan*. This is untried. It joins the best-scored imperative ('Tell Vera what to plan.': it names who hears you and is an invitation to tell her, not 'show me the plan') with the reach of 'What needs planning?', which the style lens praised because it cannot be answered 'no' and it pulls in reminders and wishes as well as weekends. It keeps the four-letter lit word at the line's end, where the eye stops and the halo stays modest, which answers the six notes that found 'planning' too heavy. Unlike 'Tell Vera our plan(s).', it does not presume a plan exists. At 28 characters it holds one line at 3rem in the widened box, and breaks evenly on the phone with text-wrap: balance.
